component_findings.artifact_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--quidra): Tagged releases v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1 each carry attached release assets (6, 6, 6, and 4 assets respectively), consistent with automated per-platform artifact publication, but no evidence was found of listing in any OS or language package manager (apt, Homebrew, Chocolatey, winget, scoop), no install-script (curl|bash) entry point, and no Docker image or version-manager (asdf/mise-style) integration.
component_findings.channel_breadth: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--quidra): Positive signals: automated, CI-gated multi-asset GitHub Releases for every tagged version; a deliberately safety-hardened library package installer (exact-tag resolution, manifest/hash verification, sandboxed asset extraction) documented in packages.md; clear, reproducible source-build instructions. Negative signals: no first-party OS/language package-manager listing found (apt/brew/choco/winget/scoop), no curl-pipe-bash installer, no Docker image, no version-manager plugin, and building from source requires several native library dev headers (libcurl, libpng, libjpeg, libtiff, libwebp) plus a pre-existing Clang 15+ install because the project intentionally does not bundle a backend toolcha

component_findings.installers: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--quidra): quidra install resolves only exact vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release tags via git, optionally downloading HTTPS platform assets (asset.<platform>) that are inspected before extraction; asset-backed installs additionally require curl and tar, and official Linux packages declare those runtime dependencies. This is the package manager for Quidra *libraries* (dnn, vision), not for installing the Quidra compiler/toolchain itself.
